images.sourceIdentification: Staurolite Fe 2 Al 9 Si 4 O 22 (OH) 2 is an iron aluminum silicate hydroxide.  It is a common metamorphic mineral that is used by geologists to determine the degree of metamorphism.  Staurolite is known for its twinned crystals that form into the shape of a cross.  The twin is a classic penetration twin where it appears as if two crystals grew into and out of each other. It actually forms two twin types; one that is nearly 90 degrees and one that is nearly 60 degrees. The 60 degree type is more common but the 90 degree type is the most sought after.  Staurolite is found in metamorphosed aluminous sedimentary rock environments.  Its name comes from the Greek, stauros meaning “cross” and lithos meaning “stone” in allusion to the common cross shaped twins of the crystals.
images.title: Staurolite
